title: Copilot Studio: share autonomous agents with end users (run-only)
summary: The briefing's roadmap dates, licensing prerequisites, sharing behaviour and documented controls are supported. One minor qualification should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance about which administrator roles can create spending policies.

claims.claim: The roadmap item is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: General Availability is targeted for January CY2027, not committed for that date.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "January CY2027"

claims.where: front matter: previewDate; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Preview is targeted for August CY2026.
claims.quote: "previewDate": "August CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), with no government cloud listed.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap platform is Web.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap lists General Availability and Preview release phases.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability", "Preview"]

claims.claim: The roadmap description says autonomous agents previously could only be used and managed by makers.
claims.quote: Previously, autonomous agents could only be used and managed by makers, limiting their reach to the people who needed them.

claims.claim: Run-only sharing is intended to let end users benefit from autonomous agents without edit permissions or ownership.
claims.quote: Run-only sharing enables makers to securely share autonomous agents with end users, allowing users to benefit from agent-driven automation without requiring edit permissions or ownership.

claims.claim: A maker can share a published autonomous agent that has triggers.
claims.quote: You can share a published agent that has triggers with users who need to run the agent by using their own credentials.

claims.claim: Run-only recipients can be individual users or security groups.
claims.quote: Enter the user name, email addresses of individual users, or security groups you want to share the agent with. Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Recipients run the shared agent using their own credentials rather than the maker's credentials.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.claim: Learn already documents run-only sharing as preview, with prerelease setup and trigger documentation.
claims.quote:
Set up a shared autonomous agent (Microsoft Copilot) (preview)

[This article is prerelease documentation and is subject to change.]

claims.where: controls[6].ui; What's changing; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The maker selects Agents > agent > Share > Can use to grant run-only access.
claims.quote:
Open the agent from the Agents page.
Select the Share ... icon near Publish on the top menu bar.
Ensure Can use appears beside the search bar.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout; controls[6].note
claims.claim: The maker copies the Copy link to set up link and sends it to recipients.
claims.quote:
Select Copy sharing link, then Copy link to set up.
Send the link to the end users you shared the autonomous agent with.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Recipients do not receive a notification when the maker shares an autonomous agent.
claims.quote: Users don't receive a notification when a maker shares an agent with them. Makers must copy and send the can use link to end users.

claims.claim: Each recipient activates the shared agent for themselves.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.claim: The recipient must connect every trigger, tool and workflow that requires their credentials before the agent can run.
claims.quote: An autonomous agent can't run until you connect every trigger, tool, and workflow that requires your credentials.

claims.claim: Recipients can edit only trigger options the maker permits through Editable by user.
claims.quote: If you're sharing this agent with others to use, choose which options users can or can't configure themselves by turning on or off Editable by user for each option.

claims.claim: Recipients cannot change the agent's instructions, tools or other authoring settings.
claims.quote: You can't change the agent's instructions, tools, or other authoring settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Users of a shared autonomous agent cannot specify or modify tool parameters.
claims.quote: Users of a shared autonomous agent can't specify or modify tool parameters.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.
claims.quote: Tool calls are invoked and executed fully with AI, based on the maker's specifications.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: A workflow used as a tool in a shared autonomous agent accepts only end-user credentials.
claims.quote: If your agent calls a workflow as a tool, that workflow can only accept end user credentials for authentication. Workflows that use any maker-only credentials aren't supported for autonomous agents.

claims.where: Scope; controls[4].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Run-only sharing requires triggers and tools configured for user authentication.
claims.quote: Before sharing, configure the agent's triggers and tools for user authentication.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totalled and billed through the hosting environment.
claims.quote: Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; controls[0].api; summary; Why it matters; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No dedicated tenant or environment admin switch for Can use sharing is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous agent "Can use" sharing admin disable approval policy. Opened authoring-share-agent, admin-sharing-controls-limits and managed-environment-sharing-limits; none identifies a dedicated Can use switch.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: User-opt-in describes the capability: makers choose sharing and recipients activate it, rather than it automatically running for recipients.
claims.quote: Recipients can use the can use link to activate the agent for themselves, connect the agent with their own credentials, and manage their permitted trigger settings.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; controls[6].note; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require recipients to have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user licence.
claims.quote: Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites say users without a licence can sign up for a trial.
claims.quote: Users who don't have a license can sign up for a trial.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects both the per-user prerequisite and consumption billing.
claims.quote:
Users you share with have a Microsoft Copilot Studio per-user license.
Each end user's autonomous agent usage is totaled and billed through the underlying environment where the agent is hosted.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited pages do not state credit rates specific to autonomous run-only usage.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness shared autonomous run only credit billing rates per user reporting. Opened authoring-share-agent and billing-credit-overview; neither gives a run-only-specific rate.

claims.claim: For the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for LLM tokens, tools and the harness itself.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits are managed through the Power Platform admin center, subject to the resource-based policy transition described later.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are managed through the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Administrators can allocate Copilot Credits to environments.
claims.quote: Administrators can allocate credits to environments and monitor usage to ensure that sufficient credits are available.

claims.claim: Variable is the appropriate factual cost category because usage is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require publication to Teams + Microsoft 365.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to Teams + Microsoft 365, with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot to be turned on.
claims.quote: Agents you want to share are published to Teams + Microsoft 365, with Make agent available in Microsoft Copilot turned on.

claims.claim: The sharing prerequisites require user authentication configured to Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: User authentication for the agent is configured to Authenticate with Microsoft.

claims.claim: Editing permissions are separate from Can use and can be assigned through environment security roles.
claims.quote: Add users to the agent's environment, and then assign users editing rights through the environment's security roles.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: End-user credentials bound the agent's actions to the recipient's permissions; the agent cannot perform an action the recipient lacks permission to perform.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The maker's instructions and tools determine what the autonomous agent does with trigger information.
claims.quote: The trigger sends event details to the agent. Your agent's instructions and tools determine what the agent does with those details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Data policies govern connectors used by Copilot Studio agents in the policy's environment scope.
claims.quote: These data policies apply to Copilot Studio agents in the environments included in the policy's scope.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not specify the effect of a policy change on an already-running shared run-only instance or trigger.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "shared" "autonomous" "data policy". Read admin-data-loss-prevention, shared-agent setup and admin-dlp-troubleshooting excerpts. General enforcement is documented, but interruption of an ongoing shared run is not specified.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Change & support
claims.claim: Maker updates can require recipients to connect services or consent to changes on the agent management page.
claims.quote: The agent owner can update the agent, which might require you to connect or consent to the updates.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Autonomous runs start from connected-service events rather than requiring a person to open a chat.
claims.quote: Autonomous agents run when an event occurs in a connected service. For example, an agent can respond when an item is created in SharePoint, an email arrives, or a scheduled time occurs.

claims.claim: No approval setting specific to run-only shared autonomous agents is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "autonomous" "approval" "shared". Opened authoring-share-agent, end-user-manage-shared-agent and guidance/autonomous-agents. Design guidance recommends human approval, but these pages document no run-only-specific approval setting.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs recipients to bookmark the agent management URL to check health, fix connections and consent to maker updates.
claims.quote: End users need to bookmark the agent management URL to check their agent's health, fix the agent, consent to maker updates to the agent, and other management tasks.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The end-user management article does not state what administrators can see of individual recipients' instances.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio shared autonomous agent data policy existing running instances administrator maker disabled credit rates per user reports. Read end-user-manage-shared-agent in full; no administrator instance visibility is stated.

claims.where: Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing and setup pages do not say what happens to recipients' instances when the maker's account is disabled.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "autonomous" "maker" "disabled" "instances". Opened authoring-share-agent and end-user-manage-shared-agent; neither states the fate of recipient instances after maker account disablement.

claims.claim: The cited pages do not explain how shared autonomous agents' per-user credit totals appear in admin reports.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Microsoft Copilot harness shared autonomous run only credit billing rates per user reporting. Read billing-credit-overview, the cited cost page and capacity-report excerpts; no shared-run per-user report presentation was specified.

claims.claim: Managed Environments sharing controls are at Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Edit Managed Environments > Manage sharing.
claims.quote:
Select Manage.
Select Environments.
Select a managed environment.
In the command bar, Edit Managed Environments.
The sharing rules are located in the Manage sharing section.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls table and notes
claims.claim: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration saves the prepared sharing configuration.
claims.quote: Set-AdminPowerAppEnvironmentGovernanceConfiguration -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId> -UpdatedGovernanceConfiguration $governanceConfiguration

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: These general sharing controls apply in Managed Environments and are documented for Editor and Viewer sharing.
claims.quote:
You configure the sharing limits for agents as a Managed Environments control in the Power Platform admin center.
You can enforce how makers share Editor or Viewer assignments with other individuals for their agents in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly confirm that Editor and Viewer sharing limits evaluate autonomous-agent Can use sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Copilot Studio" "Can use" "sharing limits". Opened managed-environment-sharing-limits and admin-sharing-controls-limits. Their rules describe Editor and Viewer permissions; authoring-share-agent describes Can use without mapping it to those rules.

claims.claim: The documented preparation retrieves the environment with Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment and reads its governanceConfiguration.
claims.quote:
$environment = Get-AdminPowerAppEnvironment -EnvironmentName <EnvironmentId>
$governanceConfiguration = $environment.Internal.properties.governanceConfiguration

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: sharing-limits PowerShell notes
claims.claim: The agent sharing example sets extendedSettings bot-limitSharingMode and bot-maxLimitUserSharing to restrict security groups and viewer counts.
claims.quote:
-Name 'bot-limitSharingMode' -Value "ExcludeSharingToSecurityGroups" -Force
-Name 'bot-maxLimitUserSharing' -Value "20" -Force

claims.claim: The data policy path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Add an environment > Available > environment > Add to policy > Assign connectors.
claims.quote:
Select Security, and then select Data and privacy.
Select Data policy.
Select New Policy.
The Add an environment page appears.
Select the environment in the Available tab, and then select Add to policy.
The Assign connectors page appears.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table and notes
claims.claim: The Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell cmdlet New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy creates a policy from the supplied object.
claims.quote:
Module: Microsoft.PowerApps.Administration.PowerShell Module
New-DlpPolicy -NewPolicy $NewPolicy
Creates a new policy with the $NewPolicy object.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: data policy notes
claims.claim: The New-DlpPolicy reference does not describe assigning the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector to Blocked.
claims.quote: Searched: the full cited New-DlpPolicy reference for Microsoft Copilot Studio, connector assignment and Blocked. Read its syntax, example and parameters; it documents policy creation but no connector-specific blocking procedure.

claims.where: controls[2].governs; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Blocking the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector in a data policy prevents makers from adding event triggers.
claims.quote: To prevent agent makers from adding event triggers to their agents ... configure a data policy that blocks the Microsoft Copilot Studio connector.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls: data policy notes
claims.claim: The documented data policy prerequisites specify tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a tenant admin or have the Environment Admin role.

claims.claim: An enforced event-trigger restriction produces a detailed error in the Triggers section.
claims.quote: If the policy is enforced, a detailed error message appears in the Triggers section on the Overview page. The message mentions the name of the data policy and suggests you contact your admin.

claims.claim: For an ungrouped environment, maker credentials are controlled at Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.
claims.quote:
Select Manage.
Select Environments or Environment groups.
Select Settings ... Expand the Product section, and select Features.
Scroll to the Copilot Studio agents section.
Under Control maker credential options, select End-user credentials or Maker-provided credentials, or both.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Control maker credential options was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio Control maker credential options Power Platform API administration PowerShell pac admin Dataverse organization settings. Opened configure-no-maker-authentication; no setting-specific automation was found.

claims.claim: Grouped environments must use Manage > Environment groups > group > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options instead of the individual environment page.
claims.quote:
You can't configure this feature on the individual details page for environments that are in a group, you must use the group's details page.
Select Environments or Environment groups.

claims.claim: Configuring the grouped-environment setting requires a tenant admin with access to the group.
claims.quote: If the environment you want to configure is part of an environment group, you must be a tenant admin with access to the group.

claims.claim: The maker credential restriction is described as immediately affecting tools for all agents in the environment.
claims.quote: The feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group. All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.claim: Microsoft warns that blocking maker-provided credentials causes scheduled or autonomously triggered background agents to fail for missing credentials.
claims.quote: Agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials. All agent triggers must involve an active user.

claims.claim: The cited embedded-credentials article documents Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote:
Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure.
Select Settings, and then select Features.
Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: No documented automation equivalent for the embedded maker credentials sharing setting was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "embedded maker credentials" "PowerShell" "API"; also the Dataverse organization Web API query. Read configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials and the Power Platform security control article; only UI procedures were documented.

claims.claim: Connections configured for end-user credentials are not subject to the embedded-maker-credentials connection-sharing restriction.
claims.quote: Connections configured to use end-user credentials aren't subject to this connection-sharing restriction because each user authenticates by using their own connection at runtime.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies are added at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote:
In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to Copilot > Cost Management.
Select Configuration, and then select Add spending policy.

claims.claim: No documented API equivalent for the resource-based agent or environment spending policy was found.
claims.quote: Searched: "resource-based" "spendingPolicies" API. Opened the cost-management API overview and read spendingPolicy reference excerpts: documented types scope all users or selected groups, not agents or environments.

claims.claim: The cited cost-management article recommends the AI Administrator role for managing spending policies.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator or Dynamics 365 Administrator | AI Administrator | Manage spending policies.
claims.fix: Keep the cited recommendation, but add: 'Microsoft's Copilot Managed Runtime licensing FAQ says Global Administrators and Billing Administrators can create spending policies, while AI Administrators and License Administrators can edit existing policies but cannot create them.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/apps/licensing-faq?view=o365-worldwide#managing-costs for this qualification.

claims.claim: Resource-based spending policies can cover selected agents or environments.
claims.quote:
Specific resource | Individual agents that you select.
Resource collection | All supported usage in the environments that you select, including apps and workflows deployed in those environments.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A resource-based spending policy can set a monthly spending limit.
claims.quote: Choose No limit or set a monthly spending limit for the policy.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: A resource-based spending policy can also set an optional per-agent limit.
claims.quote: You can also set a per-agent limit so that no single agent covered by the policy uses more than the amount you specify.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[5].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: For covered resources, the Microsoft 365 resource-based policy takes precedence and replaces Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans.
claims.quote: For resources covered by the spending policy, Copilot Credit management moves to the Microsoft 365 admin center, replacing their Power Platform admin center capacity allocations and linked billing plans.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; controls[5].note; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Resource-based policies exclude AI Builder features and their credits, and Microsoft warns against moving resources that use AI Builder to those policies.
claims.quote:
Resource-based policies created in the Microsoft 365 admin center don't apply to AI Builder features or the credits they consume.
Don't move resources, agents, workflows or environments that use AI Builder to these policies.

claims.claim: The existing Power Platform spending configuration remains in effect until a resource-based policy covers the resource.
claims.quote: To opt in, create a Microsoft 365 admin center resource-based spending policy. Until then, your existing Power Platform admin center configuration remains in effect.

claims.claim: Recipients can pause and resume triggers using the Enabled toggle on the agent management page.
claims.quote: To pause a trigger without removing its configuration, turn the Enabled toggle off. Turn it on again when you want the trigger to run.

claims.claim: The agent management page's Activity tab shows recent runs and helps identify failed runs.
claims.quote: Use the Activity tab to review recent runs and identify failed runs.

claims.claim: The documented autonomous sharing experience concerns agents built with the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: Use triggers to create autonomous agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: No documented automation equivalent for granting autonomous-agent Can use access was found.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio autonomous shared agent "Can use" Dataverse Web API permissions sharing; "Can use" "autonomous" "API" sharing. Opened authoring-share-agent and admin-sharing-controls-limits; generic Dataverse sharing results did not document this permission.
